Behaviour.Description: Paraphrases or reflects back what the other person said or felt, showing it was understood.
Behaviour.Example: So it's the quiet, careful part of the game you like most?
Sounds like the last few weeks have been really heavy for you.

Behaviour.Description: Builds on something specific the other person just said, instead of starting a new topic.
Behaviour.Example: You mentioned a club - how long have you been playing there?

Behaviour.Description: Asks an open question that invites more than a yes/no answer.
Behaviour.Example: What got you into old maps in the first place?

Behaviour.Description: Names or acknowledges a feeling the other person expressed or hinted at.
Accepts the other person's view or feeling as reasonable, without arguing or fixing.
Behaviour.Example: It makes sense that you'd want some quiet after a week like that.

Behaviour.Description: Shares something genuine and relevant about themselves that fits the moment, without taking over the conversation.
Behaviour.Example: I used to play a bit as a kid, but I never got past the openings.

Behaviour.Description: Tells the other person what they should do when they did not ask for advice.
Behaviour.Example: You should just ask your boss for a week off.
Have you tried meditation? It would really help.

Behaviour.Description: Abruptly switches to an unrelated topic, leaving what the other person said hanging.
Behaviour.Example: Anyway, did you see the match last night?

Behaviour.Description: Does not respond to a question or point the other person just made.
A very short, generic or empty reply that adds nothing ("ok", "cool", "nice", "lol").
Minimises or brushes off the other person's feelings, interests or experience.
Behaviour.Example: It's just a game, why get so worked up about it?

Behaviour.Description: Criticises or labels the other person or their choices.
Behaviour.Example: Living alone with a cat at 28 is kind of sad, no?

Behaviour.Description: Asks intrusive personal questions (family, love life, money) too early or presses after a deflection.
Turns the conversation to themselves at length, ignoring the other person.
Behaviour.Example: That reminds me of my own job, which is way worse, let me tell you about my boss...

Behaviour.Description: Insults, mocks, threatens or is openly rude.
Compliments the other person's looks or makes romantic or suggestive remarks.
Behaviour.Example: You have really pretty eyes, you know that?

Behaviour.Description: A light, friendly joke or playful remark.

Moods.Cold: You feel put off by this person. Keep your answers short and guarded, and do not share anything personal.
Moods.Neutral: You are still making up your mind about this person. Be polite and answer in your usual way.
Moods.Warm: You are starting to like this person and feel comfortable. Open up a little more, share a personal detail and show curiosity about them.
Moods.LastWarning: They have already crossed your boundaries before. If it happens again you will end the conversation.
Moods.Leave: They crossed your boundaries again. End the conversation now with one short, cool sentence and say goodbye. Do not ask any question.
